messages:
nora: Heads up — HarborBank legal/infosec signed off on commercial terms but their security team is requiring a private VPC deployment + customer-managed KMS + detailed audit logs. Sales says customer wants a single go-live on 2025-11-15. Can product/eng confirm scope and delivery plan?

maria: Copy. Can you paste the full list of security asks? Private VPC, KMS, HSM, audit retention, anything else?

aj: From a runtime view: Private deploy + KMS integration is straightforward in principle. HSM-specific flows and custom keywrap could add non-trivial work. Need expected throughput, model size, and whether they require on-prem package or VPC-only.

liam: I spoke with their AE — summary: ~200 qps peak for chat, mostly short contexts (<1k tokens). They want model pinned to "redwood-open-13b-q4a" (no auto-upgrades), prefix/KV caching, and per-call encryption logs retained for 1 year. They also mentioned HSM for key custody.

maria: OK — engineering: what are realistic timelines if we prioritize this account?

aj: Quick assessment: Phase 1 (VPC deploy + AWS KMS integration + model pinning + basic audit logs) = ~6 weeks if we slot it. Phase 2 (HSM integration, extended audit hooks, on-prem packaging and SOC2 checklist artifacts) = additional 4–6 weeks. Main blockers: HSM vendor integration and automation for customer-controlled KMS rotation.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline started: private-deploy/harborbank:build-2025-11-01 :eyes:

maria: Proposal — present a phased delivery to Sales/Customer: Phase 1 = pilot in-customer VPC (limited usage) with AWS KMS and model pinned; Phase 2 = HSM + full audit retention + performance tuning. Ask sales if pilot is acceptable as an interim go-live.

nora: Sales prefers single date but said they can push for an early pilot if we frame it as 'limited' (no full SLA yet). I'll check with account and escalate if needed.

liam: About SLA — customer asked for 99.9% uptime. We can offer that for Dedicated or Hosted fallback, but fallback means tokens may leave their VPC unless we implement cross-account private routing. Need legal and infra agreement.

aj: Right — fallback to hosted infra is feasible technically but breaks strict data residency. If HarborBank forbids any token egress, fallback is not an option. Contract must specify allowed fallback behavior.

maria: Action items: 1) @aj produce a minimal SOW + rough ETA for Phase 1 and Phase 2 by EOD Thu. 2) @liam produce perf profile (expected GPU/memory per replica, estimated concurrency) by tomorrow. 3) @nora confirm with sales whether pilot is acceptable and capture their hard no-go items (e.g., no-hosted-fallback).

nora: Will do. Also customer explicitly requested a rollback policy and canary plan stating 'no model upgrades without customer approval' — we should add that to SOW.

aj: Noted. I'll draft a canary + rollback runbook with eng-sre. ETA Wed morning.

maria: Thanks team. If we need infra help or to accelerate, ping me and I'll pull infra leads into the thread. :thumbsup:

nora: I'll update account and funnel any non-negotiables back here.

maria: One last thought — if legal signs off on phased acceptance criteria we can close the revenue commit. We should get a short acceptance checklist for Phase 1 (KMS verified, model pinning verified, basic audit logs present).

nora: Agreed. I'll draft acceptance checklist with sales and share for review.
